You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From 0a3bd5018ad72b6e9e4ea86755f8e4ecdc755ba0 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: magnum <john.magnum@hushmail.com>
Date: Mon, 25 Dec 2017 11:47:21 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] Bug fix for SAP-G format, problem introduced in 27c9bf17.
 SIMD_COEF_32 was tested before defined. Also down-tunes OMP_SCALE so it
 resembles the multiplier used for length sorting. Closes #3050.


diff --git a/src/sapG_fmt_plug.c b/src/sapG_fmt_plug.c
index f7e897106..77d0c87d2 100644
--- a/src/sapG_fmt_plug.c
+++ b/src/sapG_fmt_plug.c
@@ -25,15 +25,6 @@ john_register_one(&fmt_sapG);
 
 #if defined(_OPENMP)
 #include <omp.h>
-#ifndef OMP_SCALE
-#if defined (SIMD_COEF_32)
-// Some OMP scaling moved into max_keys, so that we can have more values in SIMD
-// mode, to sort hashes by limb size.  (TODO)
-#define OMP_SCALE               128
-#else
-#define OMP_SCALE               2048
-#endif
-#endif
 #endif
 
 #include "arch.h"
@@ -50,6 +41,14 @@ john_register_one(&fmt_sapG);
 #include "johnswap.h"
 #include "memdbg.h"
 
+#ifndef OMP_SCALE
+#if defined (SIMD_COEF_32)
+#define OMP_SCALE               32
+#else
+#define OMP_SCALE               2048
+#endif
+#endif
+
 #define FORMAT_LABEL            "sapg"
 #define FORMAT_NAME             "SAP CODVN F/G (PASSCODE)"
 #define ALGORITHM_NAME          "SHA1 " SHA1_ALGORITHM_NAME
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `src/sapG_fmt_plug.c`**
   - Removed the previous definition of `OMP_SCALE` that was set to 128 for the SIMD_COEF_32 condition and 2048 otherwise.
   - Introduced a new definition for `OMP_SCALE` where it is now set to 32 for the SIMD_COEF_32 condition and remains 2048 otherwise.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modifications in `src/sapG_fmt_plug.c` address a bug related to the `OMP_SCALE` definition that was incorrectly set before being defined. The new definition down-tunes `OMP_SCALE` for the SIMD_COEF_32 case, which is intended to improve performance and align with the multiplier used for length sorting. This change is a direct response to the issue introduced in a previous commit (27c9bf17) and aims to resolve the bug reported in issue #3050.

1. analyze the root cause of the bug in detail.
